knowledge_point.title: Finding the Points on a Curve at which the Tangent Vector is Perpendicular to a Given Vector

question.:question/problem: At which point on the curve $8 x y + 4 y^{2}=- 4 x^{2} + 5 y - 30$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $j$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$\begin{aligned}8 x y + 4 y^{2}&=- 4 x^{2} + 5 y - 30\\4 x^{2} + 8 x y + 4 y^{2} - 5 y + 30&=0\end{aligned}$$

If we set $f(x,y)=4 x^{2} + 8 x y + 4 y^{2} - 5 y + 30$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$t(x,y)=f_y(x,y)\,i-f_x(x,y)\,j$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)&=\frac{∂}{∂y}(4 x^{2} + 8 x y + 4 y^{2} - 5 y + 30)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(4 x^{2} + 8 x y + 4 y^{2} - 5 y + 30)\,j\\&=(8 x + 8 y - 5)\,i-(8 x + 8 y)\,j\end{aligned}$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $j$, we must have $t\cdot j=0.$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j&=0\\- 8 x - 8 y&=0\\y&=-x\end{aligned}$$

Substituting $y=-x$ into the equation of our curve gives:

$$\begin{aligned}4(x+(-x))^{2}-5(-x)-(-30)&=0\\5x-(-30)&=0\\5x&=-30\\x&=-6\end{aligned}$$

Finally, the corresponding point is $(-6,6)$.

curve_domain: real x,y; retain regular curve points
assumptions: tangent vector is nonzero at every included point

question.:question/problem: At which point on the curve $4 x y + 2 y^{2}=- 2 x^{2} + 2 y - 4$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $j$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$\begin{aligned}4 x y + 2 y^{2}&=- 2 x^{2} + 2 y - 4\\2 x^{2} + 4 x y + 2 y^{2} - 2 y + 4&=0\end{aligned}$$

If we set $f(x,y)=2 x^{2} + 4 x y + 2 y^{2} - 2 y + 4$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$t(x,y)=f_y(x,y)\,i-f_x(x,y)\,j$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)&=\frac{∂}{∂y}(2 x^{2} + 4 x y + 2 y^{2} - 2 y + 4)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2 x^{2} + 4 x y + 2 y^{2} - 2 y + 4)\,j\\&=(4 x + 4 y - 2)\,i-(4 x + 4 y)\,j\end{aligned}$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $j$, we must have $t\cdot j=0.$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j&=0\\- 4 x - 4 y&=0\\y&=-x\end{aligned}$$

Substituting $y=-x$ into the equation of our curve gives:

$$\begin{aligned}2(x+(-x))^{2}-2(-x)-(-4)&=0\\2x-(-4)&=0\\2x&=-4\\x&=-2\end{aligned}$$

Finally, the corresponding point is $(-2,2)$.

question.:question/problem:
At which points on the curve $x^{2} + 2 x y=6 - 7 y$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $j$?

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.

- **I.** $(-6,1)$
- **II.** $(-6,6)$
- **III.** $(-3,6)$
- **IV.** $(-1,1)$
- **V.** $(-1,6)$
- **VI.** $(1,1)$
- **VII.** $(6,-6)$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$\begin{aligned}x^{2} + 2 x y&=6 - 7 y\\x^{2} + 2 x y + 7 y - 6&=0\end{aligned}$$

If we set $f(x,y)=x^{2} + 2 x y + 7 y - 6$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$t(x,y)=f_y(x,y)\,i-f_x(x,y)\,j$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)&=\frac{∂}{∂y}(x^{2} + 2 x y + 7 y - 6)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(x^{2} + 2 x y + 7 y - 6)\,j\\&=(2 x + 7)\,i-(2 x + 2 y)\,j\end{aligned}$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $j$, we must have $t\cdot j=0.$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j&=0\\- 2 x - 2 y&=0\\x&=-y\end{aligned}$$

Substituting $x=-y$ into the equation of our curve gives:

$$\begin{aligned}(-y)^{2}+2(-y)y+(7)y-(6)&=0\\-y^{2}+(7)y-(6)&=0\\y^{2}-(7)y+(6)&=0\\(y-(1))(y-(6))&=0\\y&=1\text{ or }6\end{aligned}$$

Finally, the corresponding points are $(-1,1)$ and $(-6,6)$.

assumptions: tangent vector is nonzero at every included point

question.:question/problem:
At which points on the curve $x^{2} + 2 x y=7 y + 10$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $j$?

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.

- **I.** $(2,-5)$
- **II.** $(2,-2)$
- **III.** $(1,-2)$
- **IV.** $(5,-5)$
- **V.** $(5,-2)$
- **VI.** $(-5,-5)$
- **VII.** $(-2,2)$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$\begin{aligned}x^{2} + 2 x y&=7 y + 10\\x^{2} + 2 x y - 7 y - 10&=0\end{aligned}$$

If we set $f(x,y)=x^{2} + 2 x y - 7 y - 10$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$t(x,y)=f_y(x,y)\,i-f_x(x,y)\,j$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)&=\frac{∂}{∂y}(x^{2} + 2 x y - 7 y - 10)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(x^{2} + 2 x y - 7 y - 10)\,j\\&=(2 x - 7)\,i-(2 x + 2 y)\,j\end{aligned}$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $j$, we must have $t\cdot j=0.$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j&=0\\- 2 x - 2 y&=0\\x&=-y\end{aligned}$$

Substituting $x=-y$ into the equation of our curve gives:

$$\begin{aligned}(-y)^{2}+2(-y)y+(-7)y-(10)&=0\\-y^{2}+(-7)y-(10)&=0\\y^{2}-(-7)y+(10)&=0\\(y-(-5))(y-(-2))&=0\\y&=-5\text{ or }-2\end{aligned}$$

Finally, the corresponding points are $(5,-5)$ and $(2,-2)$.

question.:question/problem:
At which points on the curve $6 x y + 2 y^{2}=9 x^{2} + 27$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $j$?

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.

- **I.** $(-1,-3)$
- **II.** $(0,3)$
- **III.** $(\frac{1}{2},3)$
- **IV.** $(1,0)$
- **V.** $(1,\frac{3}{2})$
- **VI.** $(1,3)$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$\begin{aligned}6 x y + 2 y^{2}&=9 x^{2} + 27\\- 9 x^{2} + 6 x y + 2 y^{2} - 27&=0\end{aligned}$$

If we set $f(x,y)=- 9 x^{2} + 6 x y + 2 y^{2} - 27$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$t(x,y)=f_y(x,y)\,i-f_x(x,y)\,j$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)&=\frac{∂}{∂y}(- 9 x^{2} + 6 x y + 2 y^{2} - 27)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(- 9 x^{2} + 6 x y + 2 y^{2} - 27)\,j\\&=(6 x + 4 y)\,i-(- 18 x + 6 y)\,j\end{aligned}$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $j$, we must have $t\cdot j=0.$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j&=0\\18 x - 6 y&=0\\y&=3x\end{aligned}$$

Substituting $y=3x$ into the equation of our curve gives:

$$\begin{aligned}2(3x)^{2}+6x(3x)-9x^{2}-27&=0\\27x^{2}-27&=0\\x^{2}&=1\\x&=\pm 1\end{aligned}$$

Finally, the corresponding points are $(1,3)$ and $(-1,-3)$.

assumptions: tangent vector is nonzero at every included point

At which points on the curve $8 x y + y^{2}=16 x^{2} + 32$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $j$?

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.

- **I.** $(-1,-4)$
- **II.** $(0,4)$
- **III.** $(\frac{1}{2},4)$
- **IV.** $(1,0)$
- **V.** $(1,2)$
- **VI.** $(1,4)$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$\begin{aligned}8 x y + y^{2}&=16 x^{2} + 32\\- 16 x^{2} + 8 x y + y^{2} - 32&=0\end{aligned}$$

If we set $f(x,y)=- 16 x^{2} + 8 x y + y^{2} - 32$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$t(x,y)=f_y(x,y)\,i-f_x(x,y)\,j$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)&=\frac{∂}{∂y}(- 16 x^{2} + 8 x y + y^{2} - 32)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(- 16 x^{2} + 8 x y + y^{2} - 32)\,j\\&=(8 x + 2 y)\,i-(- 32 x + 8 y)\,j\end{aligned}$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $j$, we must have $t\cdot j=0.$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j&=0\\32 x - 8 y&=0\\y&=4x\end{aligned}$$

Substituting $y=4x$ into the equation of our curve gives:

$$\begin{aligned}1(4x)^{2}+8x(4x)-16x^{2}-32&=0\\32x^{2}-32&=0\\x^{2}&=1\\x&=\pm 1\end{aligned}$$

Finally, the corresponding points are $(1,4)$ and $(-1,-4)$.
